dialog.body: Public Works, good morning, this is Kevin.
Yeah, good morning, Kevin. Is this, uh, can you hear me alright? I got this phone turned up all the way and you still sound like you're down a well.
I hear you fine. You want me to talk up a little?

Sure, sure, of course. Hold on, there's a little button on the side here. [pause] Okay. Little better. My wife's always fooling with the volume and then I can't hear nothing. Anyway. Gino Fiore, 25 Howard Street. Fifth Ward, down near the corner there.
Howard Street, okay. Fiore. I think I talked to, is it Lucille? A couple weeks ago?
Absolutely, that's my wife. So you know the whole story already.
Some of it. Let me pull it up. [pause] Okay. Twenty-five Howard. Drain backup December, again in February. Go ahead, what happened?

Same thing, Kevin. Same exact thing. The rain Friday into Saturday, that drain on the corner backs right up again, the street fills in, water comes up to the top step of my front stoop. Top step. I'm standing in the doorway watching it like it's the ocean.
Okay. Rain ended Saturday, street ponded up to the top step. Did it get in the house?

No. No, the cellar stayed dry this time, thank God. But that's luck, that's not anything anybody did. December, after that big soaker, we got water in the cellar. Then the nor'easter end of February, again, worse. Two times this winter already. I'm not waiting for number three.
Yeah, I've got both of those here. Basement dry this time, writing that down. Street flooded to the top step.

Sure. And look, I'll be honest with you, a guy came out in December, cleaned off the grate, fine. Then end of February they came and did the thing with the hose under the street, said it was partly blocked. And then a supervisor calls my wife, calls my daughter, says oh, we're looking at a bigger fix, it's going on the engineering review. Okay. When? Nobody says when. And we've heard nothing since. Nothing. I'm still waiting on somebody to call back and tell me something.
I hear you. I'm looking and I don't see a date on the review yet, so you're not missing a call, there just isn't anything new on there.

Of course, of course. That's what I figured. Meantime, you go look at that grate on the corner right now. It's half full of sand and junk. Coffee cups, wrappers, all the sand from the plows. Half full. How's the water supposed to go down there?
Grate on the corner, half full of sand and trash. Okay. That I can put in for a cleaning, that's a quick one, separate from the big fix.
Absolutely, please. Let me ask you something else, though. Is it just us? Do you got anybody else on Howard Street calling about this? Because I can't be the only one with water at the door.

Let me check. [pause] Under Howard Street, what I'm seeing is the calls from your house. Your wife, your daughter. Doesn't mean neighbors didn't call somewhere else or get logged under the cross street, but that's what's in front of me.
Sure. Well, maybe I go knock on some doors then, get 'em to call. Because one house complaining, nobody moves. I been in that house a long time, I know how it goes.

Wouldn't hurt. More calls on the same corner does get attention. So here's what I'm doing. I'm adding Saturday's backup to the repeat file on your address, putting the grate in for cleaning, and I'm telling the supervisor directly you're still waiting to hear on the engineering piece.
Okay. And when does somebody come?
For the bigger fix, I don't have a crew date to give you. It's sitting with engineering. The grate cleaning goes on the list today, they work through those as they get to them.
Sure, of course. I've heard that one before, Kevin, no offense to you. You're the only one picks up.
None taken. Your number's on file from your wife's call, the 0107 one?
Absolutely, that's the house. Just, whoever calls, let it ring. Takes me a minute. And I gotta find the button again.
I'll put that in the note. Let it ring.
Alright. Thank you. Get that grate cleaned before the next one, huh?
I'll push it. Take care, Mr. Fiore.
